review_notice: Three public-clause categories and one user-provided workplace-policy category are eligible for automatic findings after applicability and exception checks. Eating at an operating cashier workstation is a workplace-policy violation, not an independently verified public-law claim. Loose-cash counting omission is review-only because sparse samples cannot establish a missing procedure. Other observable events remain an unconfirmed review queue.

sources.title: Cashiers must not eat at their workstation during work
sources.provenance: The user explicitly instructed that eating at the cashier workplace/table during work is a violation. This is an application workplace policy; no statutory clause or independent employer document is claimed.

rules.label: Workstation departure during unfinished cash intake
rules.document: NBK Board Resolution No. 231 of 29 November 2019
rules.summary: In the cash-intake subsection, the cashier must not leave the workstation before client service ends.
applicability: An actual client cash-intake transaction is established.
Client service has started and has not visibly completed.
The observed departure leaves the workstation, rather than merely changing posture or reaching within it.
exceptions: Departure after completed client service.
Standing, reaching, movement inside the workstation, or a brief occlusion.
Uncertain transaction type, boundaries, or workstation boundaries.
disabled_examples: Any empty chair without active intake context.
Generic absence during an unknown operation.
rules.context_requirement: Referenced pre-action, action and post-action observations must establish the relevant transaction context. Sparse observations do not prove that an action never happened.

rules.label: Client cash accepted or counted during the client's demonstrable absence
rules.document: NBK Board Resolution No. 231 of 29 November 2019
rules.summary: Acceptance and counting of client cash during intake takes place in the client's presence.
applicability: Client cash intake and the relevant cash lineage are established.
The client area is visible sufficiently to establish actual absence.
Acceptance or counting takes place during that absence.
exceptions: Client outside a crop or occluded: presence is unknown.
Cash stock preparation or preparatory payout counting rather than client intake.
Counting performed by equipment counts as counting.
disabled_examples: No visible client in a camera angle that omits the client area.
rules.context_requirement: Referenced pre-action, action and post-action observations must establish the relevant transaction context. Sparse observations do not prove that an action never happened.

rules.label: Earlier client's cash left outside storage during a new transaction
rules.document: NBK Board Resolution No. 231 of 29 November 2019
rules.summary: Only the current client's cash remains at the workstation; previously accepted cash belongs in designated key-lockable storage.
applicability: Cash accepted from an earlier client is positively identified.
The previous transaction ends and a distinct next client transaction starts.
The earlier cash remains outside designated storage, with continuity across the transition.
exceptions: Several cash piles belonging to one client.
Unidentified teller stock or ambiguous ownership.
An open drawer alone does not prove improper storage or an always-locked requirement.
disabled_examples: Open cash drawer without identified exposed earlier-client cash.
Two visible bundles whose ownership cannot be established.
rules.context_requirement: Referenced pre-action, action and post-action observations must establish the relevant transaction context. Sparse observations do not prove that an action never happened.

rules.label: Loose payout cash handed over without the required observed count
rules.document: NBK Board Resolution No. 231 of 29 November 2019
rules.summary: Prepared payout cash is counted in the client's presence before handover; paragraph 32 allows qualifying intact packages, full straps, and packaged coins to be issued by their marked amounts.
applicability: Cash payout, loose cash, and handover are established.
The complete preparation-to-handover opportunity is continuously visible.
Manual, machine, earlier, and offscreen counting are excluded by the visible complete context.
The packaging exceptions in paragraph 32 are affirmatively excluded.
exceptions: Intact full or incomplete packs and individual full straps may be issued by marked amounts.
Qualifying packaged coins may be issued by labeled amounts.
An earlier or offscreen count remains possible.
Packaging completeness or integrity is too small or occluded to determine.
disabled_examples: A single handover frame with no full transaction coverage.
An intact strap or pack handed over without unwrapping.
Counting not visible because of occlusion or a missing portion of the clip.
rules.review_only_reason: Complete preparation-to-handover counting absence cannot be established by sparse sampling; no automatic violation is emitted.

rules.label: Cup, beverage, or presumed personal property
rules.document: NBK Board Resolution No. 231 of 29 November 2019
rules.summary: The personal-property clause does not establish that a visible cup is prohibited; contents, ownership, room applicability, and exceptions remain unresolved.
exceptions: Medicines, medical devices, and qualifying communication devices are expressly excepted.
disabled_examples: Unidentified object interpreted as prohibited personal property.

rules.label: Physical identification document not visible
rules.document: NBK Board Resolution No. 231 of 29 November 2019
rules.summary: Digital identification is permitted; an unseen paper identity document does not establish failure to identify.
exceptions: Digital-documents-service data.
Identification before the clip or outside camera view.

rules.label: No separate supervisor during an ordinary client transaction
rules.document: NBK Board Resolution No. 231 of 29 November 2019
rules.summary: The supervisory-presence rule expressly excludes client cash intake and payout.
exceptions: Ordinary client intake or payout.
Role and authorization cannot be inferred from appearance.
disabled_examples: Only one teller visible during customer service.

rules.label: Open door treated as a universal violation
rules.document: NBK Board Resolution No. 14 of 24 February 2020
rules.summary: These clauses address room isolation and closable or lockable entrances; they do not establish a universal always-closed or always-locked state requirement.
exceptions: Room configuration and legal room category are unknown.
Construction capability is distinct from a momentary observed door state.
disabled_examples: Any open door in a teller video.

rules.label: Cashier eating at the workstation during work
rules.summary: Under the user-provided workplace policy, a cashier must not eat at the operating cashier workstation/table during work. Require a clearly visible food-consumption sequence such as identified food brought to the mouth and bitten or chewed, together with the person operating the cashier workstation and a visible working context such as a staffed cash desk with work activity. A single hand-to-face gesture, drinking alone, food merely present, medicine, a break-room setting, or an unresolved off-duty context does not establish this violation. Do not infer shift schedules from appearance.
applicability: The person visibly operates the cashier workstation; role follows workstation activity, not appearance or identity.
The relevant table or counter is a cashier workstation, with visible working context such as a staffed cash desk and work activity.
An identifiable food-consumption action is visible in a sequence, rather than inferred from food presence or a hand-to-face pose.
exceptions: Only drinking is observed, without visible food consumption.
Food is merely present, handled, opened or moved without visible consumption.
The movement is face touching, medicine taking or another non-food action, or remains ambiguous between those actions and eating.
The person is outside the cashier workstation, in a break area, or the relevant working context is not established.
disabled_examples: Food, a plate, a cup or a wrapper on the table without eating.
A cup raised to the mouth with no visible food consumption.
A hand near the face without identifiable food and a consumption sequence.
A person eating in a break room or an unresolved nonworking context.
rules.context_requirement: Referenced before/action/after observations must establish food consumption by the cashier at an operating workstation. Work context must be visible; shift schedules and off-duty status are not inferred. All exceptions require affirmative, referenced exclusion before a finding.
